title: Refunds
outcomes: Identify refund situations and time limits.
Compute refund of unutilised ITC on exports and inverted duty.
Apply procedure, provisional refund and withholding.
Apply unjust enrichment, interest and Consumer Welfare Fund.

meta.exam_tip: Write the rule 89 formula before substituting numbers.

concepts.title: Situations and time limit for refund
body: Section 54 allows refund of tax, interest or other amounts, including excess balance in the cash ledger, tax on zero-rated supplies, unutilised ITC on exports without tax or on inverted duty structure, tax on deemed exports, tax paid on supplies not provided, wrongly paid tax under section 77, and tax on supplies to UN bodies and embassies.

Refund of unutilised ITC is barred where goods exported are subject to export duty, or where the supplier claims drawback of central tax. Inverted duty refund is not available for notified goods or services.

An application in RFD-01 must be filed within two years from the relevant date — e.g. date of shipment for goods exports, date of receipt of payment for services exports, due date of return for inverted duty claims. The two-year limit does not apply to excess balance in the cash ledger.
concepts.analogy: Refund is available in listed situations within two years.
concepts.work: An exporter of goods files for refund within two years of the shipping date.

concepts.title: Refund of unutilised ITC — exports and inverted duty
body: Rule 89(4) for zero-rated supplies without tax: refund equals Net ITC multiplied by the share that zero-rated turnover forms of adjusted total turnover. Zero-rated goods turnover is capped at 1.5 times the value of like goods supplied domestically.

Rule 89(5) for inverted duty: maximum refund = (turnover of inverted rated supply × Net ITC ÷ adjusted total turnover) − (tax payable on such supply × Net ITC ÷ ITC on inputs and input services). Net ITC here covers inputs only, not input services or capital goods.
Credit used for computing the refund is debited from the credit ledger and restored if the claim is rejected.
concepts.analogy: Formulas share refund by turnover proportion.
concepts.work: Exports of ₹60 lakh out of ₹1 crore turnover with ₹9 lakh ITC yield ₹5.4 lakh refund.

concepts.title: Procedure, provisional refund and withholding
body: The proper officer acknowledges a complete application within 15 days and decides within 60 days of receipt. For zero-rated supplies, 90% is refunded provisionally within 7 days of acknowledgement, unless the applicant was prosecuted for a specified offence in the preceding five years.
Refunds below ₹1,000 are not paid. IGST paid on exported goods is refunded automatically once the shipping bill and GSTR-3B are validated, treating the shipping bill as the application.

Section 54(10)–(12): refund can be withheld or adjusted against unpaid demands, or withheld where an appeal is pending and fraud is suspected — with 6% interest payable if the taxpayer ultimately succeeds.
concepts.analogy: Fast provisional refunds for exporters; safeguards for revenue.
concepts.work: An exporter receives 90% of its refund within a week.

concepts.title: Unjust enrichment, interest and Consumer Welfare Fund
body: Unjust enrichment: refund is paid to the applicant only if the incidence of tax has not been passed on; otherwise it goes to the Consumer Welfare Fund (section 57). Exceptions where it is paid to the applicant include exports, deemed exports, unutilised ITC, tax on supplies not made, and wrongly paid tax under section 77.

For claims above ₹2 lakh, a CA or cost accountant certificate that incidence has not been passed on is required; for smaller claims, a self-declaration suffices. Every amount of tax paid is presumed passed on unless proved otherwise.

Section 56: interest at 6% per annum is payable if refund is not paid within 60 days of receipt of the application; 9% where refund arises from an appellate order and is paid more than 60 days after the application consequent to that order.
concepts.analogy: No double benefit — unjust enrichment goes to consumers.
concepts.work: A refund delayed beyond 60 days earns 6% interest.

illustrations.title: Refund on exports under LUT
illustrations.q: Tanya Exports made zero-rated supplies of goods under LUT of ₹60,00,000 and domestic supplies of ₹40,00,000 in a quarter. Net ITC on inputs and input services was ₹9,00,000. Compute the refund and the provisional amount.

illustrations.title: Inverted duty structure
illustrations.q: Pankaj Fabrics sells fabric taxed at 5% (turnover ₹1,00,00,000; tax payable ₹5,00,000). Inputs (yarn, chemicals) attract higher rates; Net ITC on inputs is ₹12,00,000; total ITC on inputs and input services is ₹14,00,000. Adjusted total turnover is ₹1,00,00,000. Compute the maximum refund.

head: Step
Working
rows: Turnover of inverted rated supply × Net ITC ÷ ATT = 1 crore × 12 lakh ÷ 1 crore
Tax payable × (Net ITC ÷ ITC on inputs and input services) = 5,00,000 × 12/14
solution.title: Rule 89(5)

summary: Section 54: situations; two years from relevant date.
Provisional 90% in 7 days; decide in 60 days; < ₹1,000 not paid.
Unjust enrichment; CA certificate > ₹2 lakh; CWF.
remember: Inverted duty Net ITC is inputs only.
traps: Applying the two-year limit to cash ledger excess.

viva.q: When is refund of unutilised ITC on exports barred?
viva.model: When exported goods suffer export duty or the supplier claims drawback of central tax.

viva.q: What is the cap on turnover of zero-rated goods?
viva.model: Value up to 1.5 times the domestic value of like goods supplied by the same or similar suppliers.

viva.q: How is IGST paid on exported goods refunded?
viva.model: Automatically, with the shipping bill treated as the refund application once validated.

viva.q: What is presumed about tax paid?
viva.model: That its incidence has been passed on to the buyer unless proved otherwise.

viva.q: When can refund be withheld with interest at 6%?
viva.model: When an appeal is pending and the Commissioner believes grant may hurt revenue due to fraud; interest applies if the taxpayer later succeeds.
